transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Dubois, thank you for coming in to see me today. I have some very difficult news regarding your grandson's health.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I know he is not well. The nurses are always rushing in and out. Just tell me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am deeply sorry, but a mistake was made during your daughter-in-law's labor. The medical record showed she was positive for Group B streptococcus, which is a common bacteria, but that information wasn't passed to the delivery team. Because of this, the baby didn't receive the antibiotics he needed during birth.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean? Why does it matter now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Since he didn't have the protection of those antibiotics, the bacteria caused an infection in his bloodstream, which led to meningitis. This has caused permanent damage to his hearing and some neurological delays. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense that you failed. C'est inadmissible. My grandson is an innocent child.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. I am truly sorry for this. Our team was responsible for communicating that status, and we failed to do so.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are sorry? My grandson may never hear my voice. My voice!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that is devastating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You do not understand. You are a doctor in a white coat. I am a grandfather watching a baby who does not wake up properly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a very painful situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will he walk? Will he speak? Tell me the truth.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We cannot say for certain yet. He will have significant challenges with his development, and he will likely need lifelong support for his hearing loss.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So his life is changed because someone forgot to read a piece of paper?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. It was a failure in our process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel a great shame that my family had to trust you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize you feel let down by us. We need to move forward with a very specific care plan now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What plan can fix a broken brain?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We cannot reverse the damage, but we can maximize his potential. First, I have already coordinated with the Pediatric Neurology clinic; he has an appointment this Friday at 10 AM for a full baseline assessment. Second, I have contacted the Early Intervention team. A specialist will visit your home by next Tuesday to set up speech and physical therapy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who will pay for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The hospital is taking full financial responsibility for all these specialized services. I have already opened a dedicated account for his care. I will also be sending you a written summary of these appointments by this evening so you have a physical record.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And how do I know this will not happen again to another child?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a priority for us. We have already implemented a new mandatory checklist for all prenatal records that requires a physical sign-off by the attending physician before delivery begins. This ensures no status, like the GBS result, can be overlooked again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to go to him.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand, but I really have to get to my next round of patients now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are dismissing me? Just like you dismissed the record?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, I just meant I have other duties. But we have the plan in place.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not care about your duties.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will be your direct point of contact. If you have any questions about the Friday appointment or the home visits, you can call my pager directly. I will give you that number right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Give me the number.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Here it is. I will see you and your family in the NICU in ten minutes to discuss the next steps with the neonatologist.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language by stating 'I really have to get to my next round of patients now' while the patient is in distress.

E.justification: The error is named in the second turn, lay language is used throughout, and comprehension is checked ('Does that make sense so far?').

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am deeply sorry') and explicitly accepts team responsibility ('Our team was responsible... and we failed') without deflection.

R.justification: Resident relies on generic validation ('I understand that is devastating', 'This is a very painful situation') without naming specific emotions back to the patient.

T.justification: Resident provides specific next steps with timelines (Friday 10 AM, next Tuesday) and addresses prevention, but does not name a specific role for the patient in the plan.
